# Cryptolean — metric catalogue

Every chart on cryptolean.com carries the version of the metric definition
that produced it. This file is what those versions mean. It is generated
from the source of each metric module on every build and is never edited by
hand, so it cannot describe a definition the site is not actually using.

Format: catalog-v1. Source: src/metrics/, src/resolution/.
23 metrics, 454 charts.

## Restatement

Retuning a metric rewrites every historical chart drawn with it, so each
version records whether values already published moved:

  initial    the first version. No predecessor to restate.
  additive   new output added; no value already published changed.
  restated   at least one value already published is different now.
  unclear    the module does not say. Not inferred, and not guessed.

A verdict is followed by the sentence from the module that produced it.


------------------------------------------------------------------------

Module:   src/metrics/alignment.py
Charts:   2

## match — match-v3

Phase 4 step 3 — candidate generation for cross-venue matching.

Module:   src/resolution/matching.py
Charts:   0
Restated: no

### Version history

  match-v1  2026-08-05  [initial]
      TF-IDF cosine candidates, unverified by construction.

  match-v2  2026-08-05  [unclear]
      Words and numbers separated. v1 tokenised on [a-z0-9']+, so "$4.07" became {4, 07} and "2026-07-07" became {2026, 07}. Rare digit fragments earn high IDF, so a question scored against an unrelated one purely on a shared "07" — "Will average gas prices be above $4.07?" matched "Will Argentina win on 2026-07-07?" at 0.71, above genuine same-event pairs. Numbers now carry no similarity weight; instead, two questions that both quote thresholds but share none are penalised, because "above $4.07" and "above $4.04" are different markets.

  match-v3  2026-08-05  [unclear]
      Dates stripped before numbers are read. v2 still let a date's parts become thresholds: "2026-07-05" gave 7 and 5, which then AGREED with an inflation question about 5.00% and cancelled the very penalty meant to separate them — "inflation in Brazil above 5.00%" scored 0.709 against "Will Brazil win on 2026-07-05?". Years are still read from the original text, because a year inside a date is exactly the deadline worth comparing.

## resrisk — resrisk-v2

Resolution risk as a metric module — the locked contract, plus the evidence.

Module:   src/resolution/risk_score.py
Charts:   3
Restated: yes

### Version history

  resrisk-v1  2026-08-05  [initial]
      wraps flags-v1's taxonomy and weights; adds clause extraction, absence basis, and the record basis for dispute history. Score values identical to flags-v1 — this version adds evidence, it does not re-tune.

  resrisk-v2  2026-08-05  [restated]
      follows flags-v2's word-boundary matching. SCORES MOVE, but narrowly: 4.2% of the corpus changes, mean 0.3263 -> 0.3289, rank correlation 0.995. The change is a matching fix — flags-v1's "tie" matched "parties" and credited 2,434 markets with edge-case coverage they never had. Weights unchanged. PHASE4_THRESHOLDS.md records the before/after and which flags survive a volume control. Evidence spans now come from flags.find(), the same matcher that scores, so a quoted clause cannot disagree with the number.
      -> moved: "SCORES MOVE, but narrowly: 4.2% of the corpus changes, mean 0.3263 -> 0.3289, rank correlation 0.995."
      -> unchanged: "Weights unchanged."

### Charts

  /charts/dispute-rate/  Dispute Rate by Market Category
  /charts/disputed-volume/  Disputed Volume Over Time
  /charts/repeat-disputes/  Repeat-Dispute Leaderboard

## risk — risk-v1

Risk metric — reconstruction, not a clone.

Module:   src/metrics/risk.py
Charts:   48
Restated: no

### Version history

  risk-v1  2026-08-05  [initial]
      f=0.395, ma=365d. Phase 0 gate: 6/6 on cycle-risk extremes. Deliberately not retuned to 0.625 to force the Apr-2021 price-date reading. See PHASE0_RESULT.md.
